body:
## Status

Core semantic classification issue for **Qleisli 0.3.0**.

**2026-10-02 release-boundary decision:** 0.3.0 freezes the distinction between equality/coherence/physics. The concrete catalogue of implicit coherence conveniences is deferred to **#197 (0.4.0)**.

Related:
- #15 — tensor reassociation
- #18 — owner packaging
- #27 — type-theory synthesis
- #43 — `Unit / Q<Unit>`
- #76 — binding exchange vs axis permutation vs physical SWAP
- #100 — inference law
- #196 — three-level surface boundary
- #197 — 0.4.0 boundary-condition umbrella

## Problem

Several relations can look superficially like “the same type”:

```text
((A × B) × C)  ~  (A × (B × C))
A × Unit        ~  A
Q<(A,B)>        ~  (Q<A>, Q<B>)
Bits<0>         ~  Unit
```

but Qleisli must not collapse distinct notions of sameness.

## Frozen 0.3.0 classification

The language distinguishes exactly these semantic categories:

### 1. Definitional equality

Two forms are literally the same for type checking.

No physical or structural operation is inserted.

### 2. Canonical coherence

Two forms are not definitionally identical, but there may exist a **unique theorem-justified structural map** that preserves the intended meaning.

Any map admitted as canonical coherence must preserve:

- ordered leaves/axes;
- ownership accounting;
- exact phase required by the structural law;
- surrounding/reference semantics.

### 3. Physical map

A real semantically visible transformation remains explicit.

Examples include:

- axis permutation;
- SWAP/routing with physical meaning;
- preparation;
- observation;
- discard/reset;
- nontrivial phase;
- any transformation that changes the requested quantum meaning.

## Constitutional 0.3.0 rules

0.3.0 freezes these laws:

1. **Physical maps are never ordinary coercions.**
2. **Leaf/axis permutation is never mere coherence.**
3. **Canonical coherence, when later enabled, must be unique and theorem-justified.**
4. **Coherence must not duplicate/drop owners or infer separability.**
5. **Coherence must preserve exact phase and reference behavior.**
6. **Equal physical width or equal Hilbert-space dimension does not imply type equality.**
7. **Evidence/cache identity may not silently identify semantically different interfaces.**
8. **No elaborator may choose among multiple distinct quantum meanings by preference.**

These are 0.3.0 laws independent of which conveniences 0.4.0 ultimately adopts.

## Deferred to 0.4.0 (#197)

0.4.0 decides concrete boundary policy such as:

- whether tuple associativity is definitional or elaborated coherence;
- whether unitors are implicit;
- whether `Bits<0>` is definitionally `Unit` or canonically related;
- when `Q<(A,B)>` may implicitly pack/unpack to `(Q<A>,Q<B>)`;
- which canonical maps the surface elaborator inserts automatically;
- how diagnostics expose inserted coherence;
- which canonical normal form is used for authoring and inference.

Those decisions must satisfy the 0.3.0 laws above.

## Relationship to Core

The trusted/verified Core may remain more explicit than the surface language.

A future surface coercion may elaborate to explicit structure, but:

- the elaborator does not gain semantic authority;
- the emitted structure remains independently checkable;
- source convenience must not quotient away phase, ownership or axis order in the verifier.

## Acceptance criteria for 0.3.0

- [ ] The Reference distinguishes definitional equality, canonical coherence and physical maps.
- [ ] Physical maps cannot be inserted as ordinary type coercions.
- [ ] Axis permutation is explicitly outside coherence.
- [ ] Any future canonical coherence is constrained to preserve phase, ownership and reference semantics.
- [ ] Equal width/dimension is explicitly insufficient for type/evidence identity.
- [ ] Inference cannot choose between multiple semantic maps.
- [ ] The concrete catalogue of implicit coherence maps is explicitly deferred to #197.

## Non-goals

0.3.0 does **not** need to:

- enumerate every future implicit coherence map;
- choose all tuple/unit/zero-width normalization rules;
- quotient the trusted IR by coherence;
- implement general theorem proving.

## Design principle

> **0.3.0 decides what kinds of sameness exist. 0.4.0 decides which canonical sameness conveniences become implicit.**

## 2026-10-04 target type contract

Use structural definitional equality over constructor tags, normalized static sizes, immediate tuple arity, nesting and ordered leaves. In 0.3.0, Bit differs from Bits<1>, Unit differs from Bits<0>, tuple trees retain their shape, and Q<(A,B)> differs from (Q<A>,Q<B>). Introduce no implicit coherence. Explicit checked structural maps must preserve axes, ownership and phase +1 under arbitrary references. #197 retains the later implicit-convenience catalogue.

The [target Language Reference](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/codex/v0.3.0-foundation/docs/src/reference/type-model.md) and [foundation analysis](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/codex/v0.3.0-foundation/docs/src/design/type-foundation.md) record this ordinary implementation decision under the approved 0.3.0 plan and adopted authority hierarchy. Edition remains 2026. This is not a new Guardian interpretation or guarantee admission.

Status: target rules selected; implementation and conformance remain in progress in #307. Current alpha syntax still contains CBit/CBits and general Basis polymorphism is not yet implemented. Required positive and negative tests, exact lowering/interface preservation and native acceptance evidence remain open. Documentation alone does not complete this issue.
title: 0.3.0 core: freeze definitional equality, canonical coherence, and physical-map categories
